title: Two sides of every contemplation: the bina that grasps and the chachma that wonders
overview:
Chapter four said that contemplation must go into every particular, and this book promises to explain them all. Before it does, chapter five explains how such contemplation is done without fooling oneself. Every contemplation of how something comes from nothing has two sides. The *bina* side, the "hearing", grasps fully how the *yesh* comes out of the *ayin*, and it brings joy: he feels himself getting bigger. The *chachma* side, the "sight", sees in a flash that what brings it into being is beyond all grasp, and it brings *bittul*: the more he delves, the farther away it gets, like a giant who keeps growing. The example is the orbits, the whole gigantic universe, which come from a glimmer of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; and the same holds in *Atzilus*.

The great principle is that the two come together, in exact proportion. Whoever has the understanding without the *bittul* understood nothing, and whoever claims *bittul* without the understanding is having dreams, and is no humble man at all. Rabbi Markel takes this on to the two camps he sees around him: the *ovdim* who will not study and the *maskilim* who only collect points.

sections.title: Every particular must be known: a promise, and first a warning about how
sections.summary: Contemplating in particulars needs every level of the worlds, which no other book makes available; this book promises to explain all of it. But first it must explain how to contemplate without fooling oneself.

phrases.he: (ה) והנה אחר שנתבאר שצריך להתבונן דרך פרט דוקא, הרי מן ההכרח לידע כל פרטי חילוקי המדריגות
phrases.en: we said you have to be *misbonen* in total particular things, and know all the different details

phrases.he: בכל פרטי סדרי ההשתלשלות דאבי''ע, להתבונן בהם
אשר אינם מובנים לכל מכללי התורות כו'
phrases.en: really this is not available anywhere else

blocks.text: "Chapter five is a very important chapter." It explains what a thing is from the side of *chachma* (wisdom, the first flash of an idea) and from the side of *bina* (understanding), and how the two work together in studying *Chassidus*. It belongs as well with the chapters from about 25 on, on the unity of the service.

One has to contemplate each particular and know all the details, and these, he says, are not available anywhere else: *mikelal haTorah* means the likes of *Etz Chaim*. Certainly not from the *Zohar* or the *Sefer Yetzira*; even from the works of the *Arizal* "it's not possible to understand what they're talking about." So what is the solution?

phrases.he: ויבוארו כולם בקונטרס מיוחד,
מן הצריך מכל פרט,
phrases.en: what you need from every *prat*

phrases.he: וממילא יובן למבין ויודע כמה פרטים אחרים
phrases.en: and when you understand it good, you'll automatically understand all the *pratim*, everything

blocks.title: Shaking the Megillah
blocks.text: *Vayevo'aru kulam b'kuntres meyuchad*: here you have to do what you do with the Megillah. "You know what I'm talking about?" "No, I don't." At *ha'igeres hashenis hazos* you shake the Megillah, to show this is the *igeres* they mean. So at *b'kuntres meyuchad* "you have to shake this book," to show this is the book we are talking about.

Here he promises to explain everything. "What do you mean? It's not totally everything." He says: what I am explaining is what is needed from every particular, and when you understand it well you will automatically understand all the particulars.

A very big promise: the whole of Kabbalah and *Chassidus* in this book, everything you need to do what he said in chapter four.

phrases.he: אך תחילה צריך להקדים באיכות ההתבוננות
phrases.en: he's going to explain to us the *eichus*, the how to do it

phrases.he: גם בדרך פרט,
עוד ענין אחד הצריך ביותר
לכל החפץ באמת בקרבת אלהי״ם ואינו רוצה לצאת ידי חובתו להטעות את עצמו כו'
phrases.en: if you want to really study it properly without fooling yourself, or just to be *yotzei*: "Oh yeah, I learned a *sicha* today."

blocks.text: But first, before the particulars (chapter seven to the end of the book): he told us what the *hisbonenus* is, what it is about, the *seder hishtalshelus*, and that it must be done in particular. Now he explains how it has to be done, if you want to study properly and not fool yourself, or just be *yotzei*: "Oh yeah, I learned a *sicha* today."

sections.title: The something, which lies well in the mind, and the nothing, seen in a flash
sections.summary: Every contemplation has two sides: how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*, which can be explained until it lies well in the brain, and the infinite *ayin* itself, which no explanation reaches but which flashes in the mind. That flash, like seeing an airplane fly, is more certain than any explanation.

phrases.he: והוא בהיותו ידוע
שבכל התבוננות
phrases.en: any kind of *hisbonenus*

phrases.he: בענין אלה״י דהתהוות יש מאין
בכל מקום לפי מה שהוא,
phrases.en: wherever you learn *Chassidus*, no matter what it is

phrases.he: הרי כולל ב' ענינים
הא' בחינת ביטול היש לאין,
שזהו השגת ערך הבעל גבול תחילה באיכות אופן התהוות מציאותו מאין כו'

blocks.text: Any *hisbonenus* at all, wherever you learn *Chassidus*, no matter what it is, includes two things. The first is the *bittul* of the *yesh* to the *ayin*: how the something comes out of the nothing.

phrases.he: שזה קרוב אל השכל ביותר על ידי כמה מיני הסברים ודמיונות המשלים, וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: that is possible to understand with a total understanding through all the *hesberim* and *dimyonos*, *meshalim*

phrases.he: עד שנתאמת במוח היטב
phrases.en: until it *mamash* lies good in your brain

phrases.he: (בל"א עש לייגט זיך אין מוח זייער כו')
phrases.en: it lies real good in the brain

blocks.text: How the something comes out of the nothing can be understood with a total understanding, through explanations, images and *meshalim*: in Yiddish, *es leigt zich in moach zeier*, "it lies real good in the brain." It can be explained until it *mamash* lies well in your brain.

phrases.he: והב' ענין בחינת האין האלה״י המהווה אותו
phrases.en: The other thing is to understand that when you're learning how it comes into being, there is the *inyan* of where it's coming into being from, which is the *ayin Eloki*,

phrases.he: ואיך שהוא נבדל בערך,
להיותו בלתי בעל גבול כו'
phrases.en: which is totally infinite.

phrases.he: וזהו הנעלם מעיני השכל בהשגה גמורה
phrases.en: This is not really to be understood in a total *hasaga*.

blocks.text: The other thing is where it comes into being from, the G-dly *ayin*, which is totally infinite. Infinite does not mean what most people think, an infinite number or the like: it means totally undefined. This is hidden from the eye of the intellect and cannot be grasped in a total *hasaga*.

phrases.he: רק מכל מקום יוברק כמו ברק בסקירה בעלמא במוחו
phrases.en: there should be a flash of *chachma*

phrases.he: אמיתת ענינו כמו שהוא
phrases.en: into what it really is, how it really is.

blocks.text: A flash is a matter of *chachma*; the total *hasaga* of the first side is a matter of *bina*. Even though the explanation cannot tell you what the *ayin* really is, at the same time there should be a flash of *chachma* into what it is, as it really is.

phrases.he: אבל הוא בבחינת ההעלם
phrases.en: but it's in a way of *helem*,

phrases.he: כאילו נתאמת הדבר בראיה חושיית
phrases.en: as if this thing became real to him in a physical way of seeing.

blocks.text: But it is in a way of *helem*, and yet as if the thing had become real to him by physical seeing: a mental seeing is like a physical seeing.

blocks.title: Explaining an airplane, and seeing one fly
blocks.text:
To somebody who never heard of an airplane you could explain aerodynamics and the mathematics until he understands this thing could work, like the Wright brothers: there never was an airplane, but "look, birds can fly, so we can make an airplane work."

Then there is somebody you explained nothing to, but he saw an airplane fly. "What do you mean there's no such thing as an airplane? I saw it." The one with all the explanations I can convince with better explanations that it is not possible. The one who saw it, "there's no way to convince him out of it."

So this flash, though it is in a way of *helem*, is no explanation and he does not know the *pratim* (particulars), yet in a way it is a stronger conviction than the explanation. Like the airplane: you cannot convince the guy who saw it that there is no such thing.

sections.title: The sight of chachma brings bittul, the hearing of bina brings joy
sections.summary: The flash of *chachma* is a seeing with the mind's eye; its response is *bittul*, not feeling himself and not even feeling that. The full grasp of *bina*, the hearing, brings felt joy: the more he grasps, the bigger he feels. And they run opposite: the more he delves, the more *bina* grasps and the farther away the *ayin* gets.

phrases.he: והוא ההפרש
phrases.en: that's the difference

phrases.he: בין בחינת ראיה דחכמה כח מ''ה שבנפש,
שרואה ולא בראיה חושיית כי אם ראיה שכליית
phrases.en: he sees with his mind's eye,

phrases.he: בהברקה למעלה מן השגה הגמורה
phrases.en: he sees a flash of the thing, not really in a way of chopping it in an explanation.

blocks.text: The sight of *chachma* is a seeing with the mind's eye, not a physical seeing. It is in a flash, above complete comprehension: he sees a flash of the thing, not by chopping it up in an explanation.

phrases.he: ועל כן ההתפעלות מזה אינו רק בחינת הביטול
phrases.en: is in a way of a nullification to the idea,

phrases.he: שהוא רק העדר הרגשת עצמו מכל וכל כו'
phrases.en: the lack of feeling of himself.

phrases.he: (בל"א ער ווערט צו רירט פון ארט
phrases.en: He's totally removed from feeling,

phrases.he: ואינו מרגיש גם זה גופא כו')
phrases.en: and even this he doesn't feel.

blocks.text:
The *hispaalus* from the *chachma* is a nullification to the idea, the lack of feeling of himself. In Yiddish, *er vert tzerirt fun ort*: he is totally removed from feeling, and "he doesn't even feel that he's not feeling it," because all he feels is the flash. That is the sign of the flash of *chachma*.

That is the first half of the difference the text began a few lines back, "between the sight of *chachma*", and now it goes on:

phrases.he: ובין בחינת שמיעה דבינה,
שבאה בהשגה גמורה ממש,
שהוא באיכות התהוות היש מאין כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that it is in how the something comes out from the nothing.

blocks.text: *Hasaga* is from *masig gvul*: he moves the fence into the other guy's property. A complete *hasaga* means your mind *mamash* goes into the *meshalim* and into the actual domain of the thing.

This is in how the something comes into being from nothing: as in how the worlds of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* come out of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, and the matter of the *yichuda ila'a* (the higher unity).

phrases.he: שההתפעלות מזה הוא השמחה במורגש וטוב לב
כל שמשיג יותר, יותר טוב לו,
phrases.en: The more he understands, the happier he is:

phrases.he: (בל"א עש איז זייער גוט ומחי' לנפש כו')
phrases.en: a real good thing, and a real *mechaye* for him.

phrases.he: וכל שמעמיק יותר, יותר משיג
phrases.en: And the more that he looks deeper into it, he understands more.

blocks.text: Here the *hispaalus* is the exact opposite: not that he does not feel himself, but that he feels himself more and more. The more he understands, the happier he is.

In Yiddish, *es iz zeier gut*, and *mamash* a *mechaye* for him: "Wow, I'm getting such big *hasagos*, and I'm *mamash* growing and growing with this thing." He actually feels himself getting bigger. And the deeper he looks into it, the more he understands, the more he *chapt*.

phrases.he: ובבחינת הראיה דחכמה הוא להיפוך,
phrases.en: And the *re'iya* of *chachma* is exactly opposite:

phrases.he: כל שיעמיק יותר, יותר יפלא ממנו
phrases.en: the more he looks into it, the farther away it is.

phrases.he: מהות
phrases.en: the actual what it is, not the *metzius*

phrases.he: בחינת האין האלה״י המהווה כו'

blocks.text: With the *re'iya* of *chachma* it is the exact opposite: the more he looks into it, the farther away it is.

blocks.title: The Aibershter on the second floor
blocks.text:
Somebody who doesn't know *Chassidus* thinks we live on the first floor and the *Aibershter* (G-d) on the second. Learn a little more, and the *Aibershter* lives on the tenth floor; then the Empire State Building; then "it's in the clouds"; then all the way up to the moon. Each time farther away.

To someone who didn't learn *Chassidus* the *Aibershter* is almost a physical thing, a spiritual physical thing made out of air: "we're made out of lead and the *Aibershter* is made out of helium." The more you learn *Chassidus*, the more you see it is totally, totally beyond.

And what is totally beyond is even *Malchus* of *Asiya*, never mind the higher levels. The more he delves, the farther beyond him is the *mahus*, what it actually is, as against the *metzius*, knowing its relationships.

phrases.he: בהפלאת הערך יותר ויותר כו'
phrases.en: it goes farther and farther away

phrases.he: עד שיצטער וידאג כו'
phrases.en: till it *mamash* makes him sad, and he worries that it's going farther and farther away.

phrases.he: (כמ"ש בכתבי'12)

blocks.text: Until he grieves and worries: it *mamash* makes him sad that it goes farther and farther away. "How will I ever understand this at all? How will I have a connection to this?" As is explained in the writings.

sections.title: Two opposites at once: a worried heart and joy
sections.summary: Whoever learns in particulars properly gets both at the same time: worry at how far beyond him the *ayin* is, which is where true humility comes from, and joy at what he has grasped. The humility is not "I'm not so great as Einstein", but the man who has seen Og and is shown a ten-foot giant.

phrases.he: ולפי"ז הרי בכל מעיין בדרך פרט
phrases.en: anybody who learns properly in a *derech prat*

phrases.he: יבוא לכלל ב' ענינים האלה בהתבוננות,
בהעלם וגילוי
phrases.en: in terms of the *helem* of the thing and the *giluy* of the thing

phrases.he: והתפעלות הנולד
phrases.en: the *hispaalus* that he should get out of it,

phrases.he: ב' הפכים הם,
לבו דואג בקרבו
על עוצם הפלאת ההשגה באין האלה״י המהווה כו',
והשמחה מהשגתו בכי טוב באיכות התהוות המתהווה כו'
phrases.en: at the same time he is very happy from what he understood, and how the something comes out of the nothing.

blocks.text: Anybody who learns properly, in the particular way of chapter four, will come to both: the *helem* of the *ayin* that brings into being and the *gilui* of the *yesh* that comes into being. The *hispaalus* born of it is two opposites at once.

His heart worries over how utterly beyond grasp the *ayin* is, and he feels a total nothing. That is true humility, "not from *mussar*-ing yourself out." Not "Oh, I am not so great as Einstein": that is like "Well, I'm not so tall as Magic Johnson," still some kind of a relation.

blocks.title: The circus giant, after Og
blocks.text:
A guy who saw Og, king of Bashan, is taken to the circus to see a giant, ten feet tall. "Is that a giant?" He is used to Og, who lifts up a mountain. *Moshe Rabbeinu* was eighteen feet tall, jumped eighteen feet in the air, his sword was eighteen feet, "that means fifty-four feet, and he hit the guy in the ankle."

So here: the more he understands, the more he is *batel* (nullified); the greater the wonder, the bigger the giant gets. Before, a ten-foot giant; now, "Wait a minute, if you jump fifty feet up in the air, you're just going to hit his ankle." So his heart worries within him.
Those are the two things: he *mamash* worries over how far this is from him, and at the same time he is very happy with what he understood, how the something comes out of the nothing.

sections.title: The example from the lowest level: the orbits and Malchus of Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: The whole gigantic universe, every star an atomic explosion, comes from the outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; grasping that brings joy. What that source is stays hidden: the mind only concludes that it must be so (*muchrach b'hasaga*), and the response is a "wow": I can't even imagine.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא
המתבונן דרך פרט בהתהוות הגלגלים
מאין האלה״י שהיא מבחינת כלים חיצונים דמלכות דמלכות דעשיה
שהוא רק מבחינת כלי חיצוניות, הארה דהארה לבד,
המאיר בנפש של זה הגלגל בהשגה במהווה אותו

blocks.text: Notice he takes *davka* the lowest things, something you can *mamash* see: the sun, moon and stars going around, the earth a big ball going around and around. And how this comes out of the outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, a glimmer of a glimmer only.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה גם במלאכים דבריאה דאימה מקננא כו'
phrases.en: the same thing: the *malachim* of *Beriya* have an understanding in the *bina*, which is the sky above them;

phrases.he: שמשיגים כח האלה״י דמלכות דמלכות דאצילות כו' המהווה אותם
phrases.en: they have a *hasaga* in the *koach Eloki* of *Malchus d'Malchus d'Atzilus* that is *mehaveh* them.

blocks.text: The same with the angels of *Beriya*, who understand in *bina*, the sky above them: they have a *hasaga* in the G-dly power of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* that brings them into being.

So he gave you another thing. Everybody says there is *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity). Really there is another one: this physical world, out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. Then *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*; then *Atzilus*, out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: הרי זהו המושג בהשגה,
phrases.en: this is understood in actual *hasaga*,

phrases.he: ויתפעל מגדולת הבורא
ואיך שהמה בטלים בתמידות,
כמו שכתוב וצבא השמים לך משתחווים, בסיבובם כו'

blocks.text: This is grasped in actual *hasaga*. The whole universe is so gigantic, each star like a gigantic atomic explosion, and all the power of the entire universe is like nothing compared to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת האין האלה״י דמלכות דעשיה המהווה,
נעלם מהותו מן ההשגה
רק שממילא הוא מוכרח בהשגה,
phrases.en: it's not that he actually understands what it is, it's just that the mind, the logic, dictates that it must be like that,

phrases.he: אחר התאמת אופן הענין של ההתהוות היש כו'
phrases.en: after he goes through the explanation and it's *me'umas* to him how the *yesh*, the *yesh* of the *galgalim*, is *mis'haveh*.

blocks.text: What is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* really? Its *mahus* is hidden from comprehension; we understand only the relationship of the world to it, the *metzius*. *Muchrach b'hasaga*: he does not understand what it is, but the logic dictates that it must be so.

blocks.title: The sun, a gigantic atomic explosion
blocks.text: The sun is a gigantic atomic explosion, and a tiny dot in the universe; it takes fantastic power for all those stars to go around. All of it comes from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, so the mind is compelled: what an amazing thing it must be! Not that he understands what it is: it is *muchrach b'hasaga*.

Once it is verified to him how the orbits come into being, not even from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* but from the end of its *heichalos* (chambers), the *shemarim* (waste) of the *Ofanim*, he says, "Wow, what it must be!" If this is the little bit that comes out of it, imagine what it is!

phrases.he: ובבחינת ההעלם לבד הוא מושג,
phrases.en: it's really only understood as a *muchrach b'hasaga*, in a way of *helem*, not that he actually gets it,

phrases.he: ובהפלאת הערך נבדל דוקא
phrases.en: just an amazement.

blocks.text: It is grasped only in a way of *helem*, *muchrach b'hasaga*, not that he gets it, and in total amazement. From understanding the orbits, this going around this and that around that, he gets *simcha*.

But from thinking what *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is, he gets a wow, a *pele*: "What it has to be, I can't even imagine." Not "imagine what it is": the *hispaalus* is "I can't even imagine." It is grasped as separate beyond relation, *davka*, totally removed from him.

sections.title: The same in Atzilus: what the mind sees above comprehension
sections.summary: In *Atzilus* too the relationships of the lights and the *middos* can be understood by images from below, while the true *ayin* that shines on them is seen only by the sight of the mind. If you think you have understood it, you have not: the explanation that does not point you beyond itself was not understood. The sign is a *bittul* beyond all relation, the real humility, which is not lowliness.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בהתבוננות פרטיות באצילות באורות וכלים,
כמו באצילות אור חסד שבמלכות או באצילות אור חסד שבחכמה
ואיך שנאצל
phrases.en: how it comes out in *Atzilus*:

phrases.he: יושג על דרך דמיון מאור הנאצל למטה בגילוי מהעלם העצמות
phrases.en: he understands the relationships of the *Atzilus* according to the *meshalim* down here,

blocks.text: So too in *Atzilus*: he understands the relationships, and how it is emanated, by an image of the light that comes down revealed. Again, not that he understands what *Atzilus* really is: he understands its relationships through the *meshalim* down here.

phrases.he: כמו ויאצל מן הרוח דמשה כו'
phrases.en: how *Moshe* was *ma'atzil* from his *ruach* on the *zekeinim*,

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: and the various other *meshalim*.

blocks.title: Moshe's spirit on the elders
blocks.text: Like Moshe drawing from his spirit onto the elders, when nothing was lost to Moshe; and the various other *meshalim* of the kind.

phrases.he: ויושג גם כן בענין התהוות מדות דאצילות
phrases.en: this also can be understood in *hasaga*, in the *inyan* of the *his'havus* of the *middos* of *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: גם שהן בחינת מקוריים נבדלים מן השפעה האלהי״ת בנבראים כו'
phrases.en: even though they're really *mekoriyim* which are really totally different from the actual *hashpa'a* of *Elokus* into the *Beya*.

blocks.text: He can also grasp how the *middos* of *Atzilus* come into being, though they are *mekoriyim nivdalim*: the sources of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, yet totally separate from them and having nothing to do with them. The whole of those worlds comes out only of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, not even of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת אין האמיתי המאיר עליהם מאור עצמות המאצילם,
לא יושג אף בדמיון שכל
phrases.en: That cannot even be understood with a *dimyon*;

phrases.he: כי אם בהעלם לבד,
phrases.en: just in a way of a *helem*.

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת ראית השכל שלמעלה מן השגה ותפיסא ממש
phrases.en: The *sechel* sees that there's something that's higher than the actual understanding.

blocks.text: The true *ayin* that shines on them cannot be grasped even by an image of the mind, only as hidden: *muchrach b'hasaga*, it must be so. The sight of the mind means the *sechel* sees that there is something higher than the understanding.

So at any level of *Chassidus*, understanding has two things: you understand the explanation of how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*, and you see that there is something totally higher than the understanding. "And it has to be simultaneous."

The introduction to *Etz Chaim*, and many kabbalistic and Chassidic books, tell you: if you think you actually understand, you don't understand. "What do you mean? I understand," at least in this book. He says: "Yeah, yeah, you understand the explanation," how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*; not that you should not understand, just the opposite. But you should understand that there is something beyond the understanding.

"If you don't get that, you lost the whole point." Even what you understand you are not understanding properly, because it did not point you beyond. If you didn't get how fantastically removed *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is, you didn't understand how the something came out of the nothing.

phrases.he: וכמאמר לית מחשבה תפיסא בך כו',
שהוא מחשבה דבינה כו'
phrases.en: the *machshava* of understanding;

phrases.he: דהיינו שזהו היפך ההשגה,
phrases.en: this is the opposite of the *hasaga*:

phrases.he: כי כל שמעמיק יותר, יותר מופלא הימנו
phrases.en: the more that he learns and the more that he thinks deeply into it, the more the thing is amazingly far from him:

phrases.he: עצמיות אור המאציל כו'
phrases.en: the actual selfness of the light of the *Aibershter*.

blocks.text: *Leis machshava tefisa bach*: this is the thought of *bina*, of understanding. The thought that grasps explanations does not take hold of the actual *mahus* of the thing at all.

The sight of *chachma* is the exact opposite of *hasaga*: the more he learns and the more deeply he thinks into it, the more amazingly far from him is the actual selfness of the light of the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: והסימן לזה הוא הנולד מזה, בחינת הביטול ביותר כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and the *siman* from this is that there's this fantastic humility.

blocks.title: Og, and Moshe's "Whoa, dude!"
blocks.text: The sign of it is a fantastic humility: not next to the ten-foot guy, but when he realizes what a real giant is, like Og. *Moshe Rabbeinu* went up against him only because the *Aibershter* promised to help; when he saw Og he said, "Wait a minute! Whoa! Whoa, dude! This guy is picking up mountains and throwing them at us! How are we going to fight him?" So it is total *bittul* and humility.

Most people think humility is being five feet tall next to a guy of ten. Here it is beyond relation: "I'm not even an inch tall. I'm like nothing." The whole universe with the suns is nothing next to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, never mind the light of the Emanator. "So what do I have to talk about?"

From this comes the greatest *bittul*, the real humility. What people think humbleness is, "Oh, I'm not such a big shot, I don't understand so good," is *shiflus* (lowliness), and you are not supposed to be lowly. "No, it's just the opposite": he is a big shot, he got the *hasaga* of *bina*, knows it and is happy from it. But next to the actual *hafla'a*, it is still nothing.

sections.title: Joy and bittul come together, in proportion: the great principle
sections.summary: The *bittul* of *chachma* and the joy of *bina* must come together in every contemplation, and each depends on the other: as big a shot as he becomes in understanding, so humble does he become. This is not a by-the-way; it is the central principle of all *Chassidus*.

phrases.he: ונמצא בחינת הביטול והשמחה שמסתעפים ונולדים מחכמה ובינה שבכל פרט,
בהכרח שבאים כאחד דוקא
phrases.en: it comes simultaneously

phrases.he: בכל התבוננות בכל פרט ופרט דווקא
phrases.en: any *hisbonenus* that you go through this whole book

blocks.text: So the *bittul* and the *simcha* that branch out of *chachma* and *bina* in each particular must come together, simultaneously. If they don't, you are not studying *Chassidus* properly.

This is what you see with a lot of these kabbalists: one or the other. Either the understanding, and they get to be real big shots; or they don't want to understand nothing, just a sense of *hafla'a* and humility. But with no *hasaga* there is no real *hafla'a*: "It's a false humility."

sensitivity.reason: Sweeping criticism of "a lot of these kabbalists" as either self-important or falsely humble.
sensitivity.publishable: There are those who have only one or the other. Either the understanding, and they think they are really something now. Or they don't want to understand anything, just some sense of *hafla'a* and humility; but since there is no *hasaga*, there is no real *hafla'a* either. "It's a false humility."

blocks.text: In every contemplation, in each and every particular: any *hisbonenus* you go through in this whole book goes into both of these things.

phrases.he: והא בהא תליא,
phrases.en: and one depends on the other:

phrases.he: ואם לא השמחה ביש מההשגה בטוב,
phrases.en: if he doesn't have the understanding in the *yesh*,

phrases.he: לא יבוא להפלאת וריחוק ההשגה באי''ן
phrases.en: that means he doesn't really have the *hafla'a* in the *ayin*.

blocks.text: **One depends on the other**: if you don't get one, you don't have the other either. Without the understanding in the *yesh*, he doesn't really have the *hafla'a* in the *ayin*.

blocks.question: And the one who says, "I just have the hafla'a. I'm a simple little guy; I don't need all this understanding"?
blocks.text: "Hey, how could you be a simple little guy?" Without the understanding he has no *hafla'a*: he is really a *ba'al ga'ava* (a proud man). "What do you mean? I don't think I'm something." "Yes, you do," if only a little tiny thing, because he lacks the *hasaga* of *bina*.

phrases.he: ולפי ערך השמחה כך ערך הביטול ממש,
phrases.en: According to how happy he is, that's how much the *bittul* is.

phrases.he: כי כפי ערך ההשגה במתהווה, כך ערך ההפלאה בהבדל המהווה כו'
phrases.en: Exactly according to his *hasaga* in the *his'havus hayesh*, that's exactly the *erech hafla'a* in how fantastically above us the *Aibershter* is.

blocks.text: And the *bittul* is *mamash* in the measure of the *simcha*: as happy as he is, as great a big shot as he sees he is becoming, *mamash* a master of *razei d'razin* (the secrets of secrets), so humble he gets. Exactly as his *hasaga* in how the *yesh* comes into being is the *hafla'a* at how fantastically above us the *Aibershter* is.

phrases.he: וזהו כלל גדול בכל ההתבוננות בפרט ובכלל
phrases.en: This is a *klal gadol*, this is a general principle.

blocks.text: "This is a *klal gadol*," not something said by the way: a general principle, like "Love your fellow as yourself: this is a great principle of the Torah." It is the central principle of the whole of *Chassidus*, for every contemplation, particular and general.

sections.title: Two dreams: understanding without bittul, bittul without understanding
sections.summary: Whoever thinks he grasps creation and has no *bittul* has grasped nothing; whoever imagines he is *batel* without grasping it has a *dimyon shav*, a false imagination. In the third class this becomes the two sicknesses: those who say "we are *ovdim*, you are *maskilim*", and the big shots who know only points.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן מי שנדמה לא שתופס היטב ההתהוות
ואין לו בחינת ביטול מצד המהווה, לא השיג כלום בוודאי בלי ספק
phrases.en: If you don't see any *bittul* there, then that means he didn't understand nothing.

blocks.text: One who thinks he grasps well how things come into being, and has no *bittul* toward the One who brings them into being, "didn't understand nothing." And he says it: certainly, without a doubt.

phrases.he: ומי שידמה לו בחינת הביטול בעצמו מצד הפלאת ערך המהווה כו'
phrases.en: somebody who thinks, "Well, I'm just having *bittul* because I think of the greatness of G-d,"

phrases.he: ולא השיג בכי טוב לאופן המתהוה כו',
phrases.en: and he does not know the *inyanim* of *seder hishtalshelus*:

phrases.he: דמיון שווא הוא
phrases.en: it's just a false imagination,

phrases.he: ואין לו בחינת ביטול כלל
phrases.en: and he's not humble at all.

phrases.he: כי הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: One depends on the other,

phrases.he: לפי ערך דווקא
phrases.en: it's exactly according to the *erech*; it's commensurate.

phrases.he: מטעם הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Somebody who thinks, "Well, I'm just having *bittul* because I think of the greatness of G-d," and does not know the *seder hishtalshelus*: it is a *dimyon shav*, a false imagination. He has no *bittul* at all; he is not a humble guy.

**One depends on the other**, exactly by measure. "It's commensurate. Is that what you call it?" As much as you understand in *Chassidus*, so humble you are; as *batel* as you are, so much you understand: in direct proportion to each other.

blocks.title: Motel the humble and the sixth aliya
blocks.text: The next class opens with a student's story about humility. In a certain *shtibel* there was Motel der Anav, Motel the humble, known as very humble, who always had the sixth *aliya*. One Shabbos they gave it to somebody else, and after *shul* he threw a whole big tantrum, on and on: "You know that I get the sixth *aliya*!" Finally they told him, "We thought you're Motel the humble. Where's your *anivus* (humility)?" He said, "I am an *anav*. Next to G-d I'm nothing. But next to this *patz*?"
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 062 opens with this, a student's question on the humility point of the previous class, before it rereads these lines.

sensitivity.reason: The punchline uses a coarse Yiddish insult.
sensitivity.publishable: The next class opens with a student's story about humility. In a certain *shtibel* there was Motel der Anav, Motel the humble, known as very humble, who always had the sixth *aliya*. One Shabbos they gave it to somebody else, and after *shul* he threw a whole big tantrum, on and on: "You know that I get the sixth *aliya*!" Finally they told him, "We thought you're Motel the humble. Where's your *anivus* (humility)?" He said, "I am an *anav*. Next to G-d I'm nothing. But next to this fellow?"

blocks.text:
"That's not really what I meant." Nothing compared to G-d but something compared to somebody is not a real *anav*. Know the greatness of the *Aibershter* and you are *mamash* nothing.

And *Tanya* says straight, *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him): whatever the reason, the *Aibershter* gave this guy the sixth *aliya*. "Even if somebody curses you out, it's the *Aibershter* cursing you out"; get upset, and you are literally upset at the *Aibershter*. It is a lack of understanding. But humbleness does not mean weakness: *Moshe Rabbeinu* was very strong when somebody came up against him.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 062, answering the student's story before it rereads these lines.

blocks.title: The sixty-fourth brain
blocks.text: The brains open up into thirty-two and thirty-two, sixty-four. A *talmid chacham* may have no more than a sixty-fourth of *ga'ava* (pride); more, and he is called coarse. Why not nothing? "His heart was lifted up in the ways of G-d": the sixty-fourth brain, total infinite *ga'ava*, is the actual brain of humility, "which proves that he's humble."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 062, before it rereads these lines; it leads into his reading of them.

blocks.title: Let the one who boasts boast
blocks.text:
One should not *shvitz* (boast): not the wise man, the mighty, the rich. And mighty "doesn't mean like the Terminator": who is mighty? He who conquers his inclination; rich, he who is happy with his lot; wise, he who learns from every man. Even about that you may not *shvitz*.

Then: "in this let the one who boasts boast," *mamash* a *shvitzer*, the sixty-fourth brain. "Doesn't say it's okay to *shvitz*, he says he should *shvitz*!" In "understanding and knowing Me": knowing *Chassidus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 062, before it rereads these lines.

blocks.text: This is what chapter five says: without "a total megalomania" on one side, there is no *anivus* on the other. He has the *hasaga* of *bina*, knows it, is happy from it, knows it makes him bigger, a bigger and bigger ego from the side of *bina*. And "one depends on the other": as much as "I know the *seder hishtalshelus*," so much *bittul*.
He goes further: one without the other he calls a *dimyon shav*, "and he has no *bittul* at all; for one depends on the other," commensurate.
These are the two sicknesses. *Kuntres HaHispaalus* (the Tract on Ecstasy) describes all kinds, but the two basic ones are *bina* without *chachma*, and *chachma* without *bina*.

There are two types. Some say they are *ovdim* (those who serve G-d) and we are *maskilim* (people of intellect), and these are the most refined: "The real thing is *avoda*, and you're just into *hasagos*." But with no *hasaga* there is no *bittul*, and, as the chapters up to here explain, with no *hisbonenus* no *avoda*. "They're not *ovdim* at all."

sensitivity.reason: Dismisses a camp within Chassidus (those who stress avoda over study) as having no avoda and no bittul at all.
sensitivity.publishable: Some say, "The real thing is *avoda* (divine service), and you're just into *hasagos*." But with no *hasaga* there is no *bittul*, and, as the chapters up to here explain, with no *hisbonenus* no *avoda*.

blocks.text: Somebody says, "Oh, I'm *batel* to the Rebbe. What do I need to study this stuff for?" So you're not *batel* to the Rebbe, and not to the *Aibershter*. "It's all *dimyonos shav*. You're having dreams." "The Rebbe is *Chassidus*": if you don't want to know the *pratim* of *Chassidus*, you don't really want to know about the Rebbe.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks those who claim bittul to the Rebbe instead of study as dreamers.
sensitivity.publishable: Someone may say, "I'm *batel* to the Rebbe; what do I need to study this for?" But the Rebbe is *Chassidus*: not wanting to know its *pratim* means not really wanting to know the Rebbe, and without them there is no *bittul* to the Rebbe or to the *Aibershter*.

blocks.text: The actual verse: "Thus says G-d: Let not the wise man boast of his wisdom, nor the mighty man of his might, nor the rich man of his riches; but in this let the one who boasts boast: understanding and knowing Me, that I am *Havaya*, who does kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth, for in these I delight, says G-d." "That's what I wanted": "in these I delight" means those people.

It goes further: righteousness and justice are also *halacha*. What would that have to do with it? *Ki* has four meanings, and here it continues: know Me, that I am *Havaya* all the way up, who does righteousness and justice in the earth all the way down; "for in these I delight": these things down here are what I wanted up there. The *ratzon* (will) in the *Atzmus* (the Essence) spells out all the way down, "the end of the deed is first in thought": the whole *seder hishtalshelus*, known not in a mechanistic way, but as *mamash* the *Aibershter*, what He wanted.

Notice: "in this let the one who boasts boast." He doesn't say it's okay; he says you should. The other things are not okay, and this you should do, like a *mitzva*: not "Oh, well, if you want to, then it's okay."

The biggest criticism is: "Eh, what do you need to study this stuff? You need to be *batel* to the Rebbe, you have to have *hiskashrus* (connection to the Rebbe)." The answer: without the *hasaga* of *bina* you absolutely don't have the *bittul*.

sensitivity.reason: Part of his polemic against a camp within Chassidus that prefers hiskashrus to study.
sensitivity.publishable: One may hear: "What do you need to study this for? You need to be *batel* to the Rebbe, you need *hiskashrus* (connection to the Rebbe)." The answer: without the *hasaga* of *bina* there is no *bittul*.

blocks.text: On the other side: "Why do you have to study that? Now you have to study *Ayin Beis*." They have *bina* without *bittul*, and having no *bittul* shows they don't understand what they study, so no *bina* either. These are the big shots of *Chassidus*, and they are *Olam HaNekudim*, the world of points: fantastic amounts of points, and they can't put them together.

sensitivity.reason: Ridicules the learned "big shots of Chassidus" as a world of disconnected points.
sensitivity.publishable: There is also the opposite mistake: *bina* without *bittul*. Having no *bittul* shows one does not understand what he studies, so no *bina* either: a great many separate points that cannot be put together, like *Olam HaNekudim*, the world of points.

sections.title: Many fool themselves: the higher, the more real; and the face-kvetchers
sections.summary: Many who were raised on *Chassidus* fool themselves about humility. The fourth class takes the two mistakes apart: for those with only *bina*, the higher worlds are abstract, when the higher you go the more real it gets and the greater the *hafla'a*; those with only *bittul* are not sure who is bigger, they or the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: וכידוע לכל טועמי טעם בהתבוננות באמת
phrases.en: as is known to anybody who's a *toem taam hisbonenus be'emes*,

phrases.he: ואינם מטעים את עצמו כלל
phrases.en: and they don't fool themselves;

phrases.he: וכאשר יובן כל זה לרגילים בדברי חסידות מנעוריהם כו'
phrases.en: and this is understood to anybody who knows *Chassidus* from his young age;

phrases.he: ורבים מאד יטעו בעצמם בכל זה
phrases.en: and many people make a whole big *ta'us* in themselves,

phrases.he: בכמה אופנים שונים וכו'):
phrases.en: in all kinds of different ways.

blocks.text: As anyone who has truly tasted *hisbonenus*, and does not fool himself, knows, and as those raised on *Chassidus* from their youth understand: very many make a mistake in themselves in all this. They think they know *Chassidus* and think they are humble, in many different ways.

Humility is not *shiflus*. *Moshe Rabbeinu*, the humblest of men, acted like a king and got mad if they didn't listen. "What kind of humility is this?" He compared himself with the *Aibershter*, not ignoring his own level.

Here it is the opposite of what they think: no big shot in *Chassidus*, then no simple guy either, no "simpleton who believes every word," no "little nothing that just believes in G-d": "No, you're not, because you don't know no *Chassidus*." One depends on the other.

This also fits with what comes later. It is the *simcha* of *bina* and the *bittul* of *chachma*, and belongs with the chapters on the constant *yichud* of *Abba* (*chachma*) and *Ima* (*bina*): "two friends that never leave each other." Without *bina* you don't have *chachma*, without *chachma* you don't have *bina*: neither just the understanding nor just a *bittul* of *chachma*.
Like what these idiots are saying: "Oh, just blank out your mind." And that's *chachma*? "There ain't no *chachma* without *bina*." One depends on the other.

sensitivity.reason: Calls those who teach emptying the mind (meditation practices) idiots.
sensitivity.publishable: Some say, "Just blank out your mind." Is that *chachma*? There is no *chachma* without *bina*. One depends on the other.

blocks.title: Ice cream for the Aibershter
blocks.text: The original *ratzon* of the *Atzmus* is *davka* for the physical: not any of the worlds, but the Jew putting on *tefillin*, "a physical ice cream for the *Aibershter*." In fact "the *Aibershter* *mamash* wants to eat an ice cream," so He gave us the laws of *kashrus*, to taste one with a *bracha*. "So what did He have to come up with an ice cream for?" "'Cause He wanted ice cream. He likes ice cream." No: there should be a physical *taanug* (delight) to make the *bracha* on.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49). The tape opens mid-thought, picking up from 062 the will in the *Atzmus* for the physical (the *sof maaseh* of 062).

sensitivity.reason: Strong anthropomorphic humor: G-d "mamash wants to eat an ice cream" and gave the laws of kashrus so He can taste one.
sensitivity.publishable: The original *ratzon* of the *Atzmus* is *davka* for the physical: not any of the worlds, but the Jew putting on *tefillin*; and not just *tefillin*. He gave us the laws of *kashrus* and a *bracha* to make, so that there should be a physical *taanug* (delight) to make the *bracha* on.

blocks.title: Chazir and ice cream
blocks.text: Water has no taste, so unless you are really thirsty you make no *bracha* on it: drink it to get down an aspirin, no *bracha*. *Hanaa* means a physical pleasure, like ice cream, and on that you make a *bracha*, "because you're giving the *Aibershter* a physical pleasure." "He gets a terrible pain out of having to eat a piece of *chazir*, and He gets a great pleasure out of eating the ice cream."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Continues the anthropomorphic humor: G-d gets a terrible pain from eating chazir and great pleasure from eating the ice cream.
sensitivity.publishable: Water has no taste, so unless you are really thirsty you make no *bracha* on it: drink it to get down an aspirin, no *bracha*. *Hanaa* means a physical pleasure, like ice cream, and on that you make a *bracha*, because through it the *Aibershter* has pleasure from the physical.
sensitivity.publishableTitle: Water, ice cream and a bracha

blocks.text: This is the sickness of those who have the *bina*, all the particular points, without the *chachma* of seeing past it, how it all gets put together so that you see something beyond the whole thing. They say, "What do you mean? We see that there's something beyond this whole thing. Our whole method is that it's all abstract."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: The bachur in the fourth-year class
blocks.text:
"I'll tell you what happened once." A *bachur* told Rabbi Markel that *meshalim*, physicalizing the concepts, are for the first-year class, and he is in the fourth-year class.

But remember chapter four: you start with the orbits and see how it goes up to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and from this comes a fantastic sense of *bittul*. By them there is no sense of *bittul*, because by them *Malchus* of *Asiya* is less than the orbits.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: What the sun is worth
blocks.text: Take the sun: get its energy and you could be a zillionaire. "What do the Arabs have? The Arabs have energy," the oil; that's the whole thing they have. Some people are totally bugged out over money: tell them, "I can give you ten million dollars," and they'll go out of their *keilim*. The sun is worth more than that.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: "The Arabs" as a nation whose whole wealth is oil, beside a remark about people "bugged out" over money.
sensitivity.publishable: Take the sun: get its energy and you could be a zillionaire. Whole countries are rich from oil, and oil is energy. Tell people, "I can give you ten million dollars," and they'll go out of their *keilim*. The sun is worth more than that.

blocks.title: Buying sunlight at the supermarket
blocks.text: A dam makes millions of dollars from a little bit of sunlight, which evaporates the sea water and brings it up the hill. A hurricane does ten million dollars of damage, and you can harness the wind with electrical windmills. As he explains later in the book, all our *parnasa* (livelihood) is from the climate: not just the price of oranges, everything in the supermarket came from the sun. "You're buying transformed sunlight that your body can use for energy. That's all you're paying for." And that is one teeny little ray out of the whole 360 degrees.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So this is the *hisbonenus*: look how great the sun is. And the sun is less than a mustard seed in the universe: put a mustard seed on your property, and the sun is less than that to even this galaxy. Not the numbers of the molecules, just the number of the stars "will boggle the human mind."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: And all of this comes out of the *Shemarei Ofanim*: not even actually coming out, but induced by them, "like a magnet", not their actual power.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: And the *Shemarei Ofanim* are just the *shemarim*: "their excretion," from their sewer system. Not even the whole sewer system: a speck of it brings our whole universe into being.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Renders shemarim, the dregs of the Ofanim, as excretion from their sewer system.
sensitivity.publishable: And the *Shemarei Ofanim* are just the *shemarim*, the dregs; and not even all of them: a speck of their dregs brings our whole universe into being.

blocks.text: And that is only the *heichalos* of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, its total externality, not yet *Malchus* of *Asiya* itself. You can count the angels in a troop, but "His troops are without number"; all of them are in one *heichal*, a troop is not even a mustard seed in it, and the *heichal* is one of many.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So are we talking about an abstract thing? No: "We're talking that the power of the sun is coming from there." It is not abstract.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: The emperor who wanted to see the lion
blocks.text:
Analyzed like that, even an angel: there is a story in the *Gemara*. The emperor, "I don't remember which emperor", saw the verse "A lion roars, who will not fear?" and called the rabbis: "Your Torah is full of nonsense. Who's scared of a lion's roar?" He had heard lions at the circuses where they threw people to them. They told him it means the upper lion. "Tell him to come here." "If he'll come here, the whole world will be destroyed." "Either you tell him to come here or I'll make decrees against the Jews." "Okay, but we warned you."

The lion took one step: an earthquake, things falling down, the emperor struck speechless. Another step, and almost the whole city was destroyed. "No, no, tell him to go back." "And this is just an angel."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: And the *bachur* thinks *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is an abstract concept. Rabbi Markel told him, "No, no, it's more physical than we are." Not that it is *gashmi* (material): as far as actual energy goes, which is what we are made from.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49). Rabbi Markel is answering the *bachur* of the story of the fourth-year class.

blocks.title: The atom and the telephone
blocks.text: Any scientist will tell you an atom is an *or* (light) inside a *kli* (vessel): a bunch of energy and something holding it together. An atomic explosion does not even let the light out of the vessel. It is just a tiny bit of the energy that holds the atom together, the nucleus; not the power inside the nucleus, just the power holding its pieces together. And that is an amazing power. "The telephone that I'm holding": if I knew how to open up the *kli*, just the power holding its atoms together, "I could blow up the whole universe." We are made from energy.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light): "Oh, it's a *mashal*," like the radiance of the sun, not an actual light. Or *chachma*, which "lights up a concept"; or *chesed*, "the world is built on *chesed*". That is the *mahus*, as against the *metzius*, and "that's basically what chapter 5 is about": *bina* understands into the *metzius*, and *chachma* gets the *bittul* from an insight into the *mahus*. The *hasaga* is into the *metzius*, the *hafla'a* into the *mahus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So what is the *hafla'a*? Look at even *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*: get it to be your *gvir* (rich patron), and how many millions! How much has he got in the bank? "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold." "Oh no, that means *chesed* and *gevura*." "No, that means money, man." If the *Aibershter* wanted, right now He could give us a billion dollars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: A nickel from Bill Gates
blocks.text: And that is an insult: to say the *Aibershter* can give us a billion dollars is like saying Bill Gates could give you a nickel. You'll go to Bill Gates for a nickel? It would *mamash* insult him: "What, are you insulting me? You're taking up my time with nonsense?"
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: They see the hidden world as some kind of abstract thing. It is not like that: up there there is more *mahus*, not less. The whole energy and value of the world, whatever has value here, like gold, or what the stock market works on: go up, as in the first *hisbonenus*, from this earth to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and "there's more money."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: More streets up there, and dragons
blocks.text:
"And there's more streets." "More what?" "Streets, like you live on a street." The street came from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and not all the streets came down, as not all the light came out of the sun. Up there are more streets, houses, people, bodies, and animals we don't even have.

All the fantasy worlds have to be up there too, "like the Star Wars world": not that it came into existence, but *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* could make it, with all those creatures. In fact they exist on the next level up from the physical plane, the demon worlds, the world of the imagination, the dream world. "We don't have dragons, but over there they do have dragons."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So they have it "totally upside down," because they lack the proper *hasaga* into the *meshalim*: "the higher you go, the more real it gets." That is the first thing the *Rambam* says: He is the real reality, the real *metzius*, and all *metzius* comes from His. This world is a shadow, not even, a shadow of a shadow; the closer to His reality, the more real, and there is more stuff up there. "Yeah, but you're making it physical." It does not mean it is physical up there, but there is more up there, "because the whole down here is coming from up there."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: *Bina* is like *machshava* (thought), *dibur* (speech), *maaseh* (action), and He says, "My thoughts are not your thoughts." Your thought can't make a thing exist; "My thought can actually bring a sun into being." So in the thought is more energy than in the sun, actual physical energy, and higher, so that, as in chapter ten, you can't call it physical, or spiritual, or even *chachma*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So they have it backwards. Without the *hasaga* of *bina* they have no sight of *chachma*, and so no *hafla'a*: by them, as you go up it gets less, "because there's nothing up there."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.title: The Grand Canyon and a herd of elephants
blocks.text: Learn it properly and you know what a *hafla'a* is: going to the Grand Canyon; seeing Og king of Bashan, a *hafla'a* and a *bittul*; standing there while a herd of elephants runs through the town. That is the matter of *hafla'a*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: Going up, they didn't do the proper *hisbonenus*: if the orbits are so big and come only from the *Sarei Ofanim*, imagine how big the *Sarei Ofanim* are. The *Midrash* says it explicitly: up there it is all the more so, not some far abstract thing. The more he delves, the more amazingly far: "How much money does this guy have?" "Owner of heaven and earth." How much energy can you put up there?
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49), quoting line 38.

blocks.title: Two raging bulls
blocks.text: Somebody was going to think of the greatness and power of the *Aibershter*, so he thought of a raging bull running with all its power, knocking things down. "No, that can't be enough for the *Aibershter*." So: two raging bulls. And the people laughing at this are doing exactly the same thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

blocks.text: So they have *dimyonos shav*. And now the other side: not the big *maskilim*, but the guys with the *bittul* and without the *hasagos*, "the face-kvetchers." Look a little inside their brain and you see "they're not really sure who's bigger, them or the *Aibershter*": after all, the *Aibershter* is an *Aibershter*, but they have a *yetzer hara* which they conquered so good. The whole thing is *dimyonos shav*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Mocks a type within the Chassidic world ("face-kvetchers") as unsure whether they or G-d is bigger.
sensitivity.publishable: So both mistakes are *dimyonos shav*. And there is the other side: those with the *bittul* and without the *hasagos*. Without the *hasaga*, one can come to think a great deal of himself, of how well he has conquered his *yetzer hara*; the whole thing is *dimyonos shav*.

blocks.title: The satiated lion
blocks.text: Even the way they conquered the *yetzer hara*: they fed him so good that he doesn't bother them. "What they have is a satiated lion": keep feeding a lion a whole bunch of stuff and he'll leave you alone.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: Continues the mockery of the same type: their victory over the yetzer hara is only a fed lion.
sensitivity.publishable: There is a way of conquering the *yetzer hara* that only feeds him so well that he doesn't bother you: "a satiated lion." Keep feeding a lion a whole bunch of stuff and he'll leave you alone.

blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe's beinoni and Yekusiel Liepler
blocks.text:
These people are at least *beinonim*, at least in their own eyes; if they're making a mistake, actually *tzaddikim*, or maybe a *beinoni* who studies all the time. Like Rava, who thought he was a *beinoni*; or a *beinoni* like the *Alter Rebbe*.

The *Alter Rebbe* said, "I'm a *beinoni*." Yekusiel Liepler told him, "I know that I'm a *beinoni*. If you're a *beinoni*, that would make me nothing. So how could you say that?" The *Alter Rebbe* told him there are different levels of *beinonim*. So they are a *beinoni* at least like the *Alter Rebbe*, "not like Yekusiel."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49).

sensitivity.reason: The story is told to mock the same type as rating themselves beinonim on the Alter Rebbe's level.
sensitivity.publishable: The *Alter Rebbe* said, "I'm a *beinoni*." Yekusiel Liepler told him, "I know that I'm a *beinoni*. If you're a *beinoni*, that would make me nothing. So how could you say that?" The *Alter Rebbe* told him there are different levels of *beinonim*. Like Rava, who thought he was a *beinoni*: that kind of *beinoni*.

blocks.text: Their criticism of us: they're *ovdim* and we are *maskilim*, and not only *maskilim* but arrogant people in a *razi li* thing, "my secret is mine": all we want is a false sense of being kabbalists, "almost like a kosher Jewish hermetic kabbalists," to do magic, concerned with powers, "or whatever kind of crazy thing they want to come up with." (The tape ends here.)
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 063 reads no line: a free discussion of the chapter's two mistakes (lines 45-49); the end of the tape.

sensitivity.reason: Part of the polemic between camps; their charges against "us" are dismissed as crazy.
sensitivity.publishable: The criticism one hears of those who study is that they are *maskilim*, not *ovdim*; that they are after *razi li*, "my secret is mine", a false sense of being kabbalists, of powers and magic.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the two sides of every contemplation, and which one can be explained until "it lies real good in the brain"?
How can a flash that gives no particulars be a stronger conviction than an explanation? Use the airplane.
What is the *hispaalus* of the sight of *chachma*, and what is the *hispaalus* of the hearing of *bina*? Why are they opposites?
Why is true humility not "I'm not so great as Einstein"? What does the man who saw Og say at the circus?
What does *muchrach b'hasaga* mean, in the example of the orbits and *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*?
Why is the one who says "I'm a simple guy who just believes, I don't need the understanding" not humble, and why is the one with understanding and no *bittul* not understanding?
